vocabulary.meaning_en: a word for a person, place, thing or idea
a general name for everyday things (house, girl, camera)
the name of a specific person, place or thing; it starts with a capital letter
vocabulary.note_en: Always starts with a capital letter.
vocabulary.example: "Toronto" and "the Grand Canyon" are proper nouns.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a noun for more than one thing
a plural that does not add -s or -es (foot → feet)
vocabulary.example: Tooth → teeth is an irregular plural.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a noun you can see, hear, smell, taste or touch
vocabulary.example: An apple is a concrete noun.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a noun for an idea or feeling you can't touch (anger, democracy)
one noun for a group (team, crowd, committee)
a noun made of two words (bookstore, mother-in-law)
vocabulary.note_ar: قد يُكتب كلمة واحدة أو بشرطة أو كلمتين
vocabulary.note_en: It can be one word, hyphenated, or two words.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a noun you can count (one apple, two apples)
a noun you measure, not count (water, salt, money)
vocabulary.example: Can I have some salt, please?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a group of people who meet to decide things
vocabulary.note_ar: حروف مزدوجة: mm و tt و ee
vocabulary.example: The safety committee meets every month.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to trust or rely on someone
vocabulary.example: I can always count on my brother.

fine_lines.title: common vs proper noun
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاسم العام عادي وعام ويُكتب بحرف صغير (house). اسم العلَم محدد ويبدأ بحرف كبير (the White House).
fine_lines.explanation_en: A common noun is general, with a small letter (house). A proper noun is specific, with a capital letter (the White House).

examples.sentence: a girl, a canyon, a camera
Nino, the Grand Canyon, a Nikon camera

fine_lines.title: concrete vs abstract noun
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المحسوس تدركه بحواسك الخمس (apple, rose). المعنوي فكرة أو شعور لا تلمسه، لكن ترى أمثلة عليه (anger, democracy).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Concrete: you can sense it with your five senses (apple, rose). Abstract: an idea or feeling you can't touch, but you can see examples of it (anger, democracy).

examples.sentence: His anger was clear on his red face.

fine_lines.title: countable vs uncountable
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المعدود نعدّه (a/an أو أرقام). غير المعدود نقيس كميته (some, a lot of).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Countable: we count it (a/an or numbers). Uncountable: we measure the amount (some, a lot of).

fine_lines.title: fish/fishes, people/peoples
fine_lines.explanation_ar: fish مفرد وجمع معًا، و fishes لأنواع مختلفة من السمك. people جمع person، و peoples للشعوب المختلفة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Fish is both singular and plural; fishes means different kinds of fish. People is the plural of person; peoples means different nations or groups.

examples.sentence: There are many fish in the lake.

expressions.meaning_en: I trust you to help me.
expressions.example: Thanks for coming. I knew I could count on you.

expressions.meaning_en: one item made of two parts
expressions.example: I bought a new pair of glasses.

expressions.phrase: Give yourself a pat on the back.
expressions.example: You finished the course. Give yourself a pat on the back!

grammar.title: Ten types of nouns
grammar.explanation_ar: 1) عام 2) علَم 3) مفرد 4) جمع (قياسي وشاذ) 5) محسوس 6) معنوي 7) جمع لمجموعة (collective) 8) مركّب 9) معدود 10) غير معدود. الاسم الواحد قد يكون من أكثر من نوع: apples = عام ومحسوس وجمع ومعدود.
grammar.explanation_en: 1) common 2) proper 3) singular 4) plural (regular and irregular) 5) concrete 6) abstract 7) collective 8) compound 9) countable 10) uncountable. One noun can be several types: apples = common, concrete, plural, countable.

grammar.title: Regular and irregular plurals
grammar.explanation_ar: القياسي: نضيف s أو es (cat → cats, box → boxes). الشاذ: تتغير الكلمة (foot → feet, tooth → teeth, person → people). persons تظهر فقط في الوثائق القانونية واللافتات.
grammar.explanation_en: Regular: add -s or -es (cat → cats, box → boxes). Irregular: the word changes (foot → feet, tooth → teeth, person → people). "Persons" appears only in legal documents and signs.

grammar.title: Collective nouns are singular
grammar.explanation_ar: الاسم الجماعي يدل على مجموعة لكنه مفرد: a team, the crowd. وجمعه teams يعني عدة فرق.
grammar.explanation_en: A collective noun means a group, but it is a singular noun: a team, the crowd. Teams means several groups.
examples: There were two teams in the final.

grammar.title: Plural-looking singular items: pants, glasses, shorts
grammar.explanation_ar: pants و glasses و shorts تنتهي بـ s لكنها قطعة واحدة مكوّنة من جزأين. نقول a pair of glasses.
grammar.explanation_en: Pants, glasses and shorts end in -s, but each is one item made of two parts. We say a pair of glasses.
examples: I left my glasses at home. (one item)

questions.question: Toronto, Nino and Ford are ___ nouns.
questions.explanation_en: Specific names with a capital: proper.

questions.question: Which noun is concrete?
questions.explanation_en: You can see and touch an apple.

questions.question: "I left my glasses at home." How many items?
questions.explanation_en: Glasses is one item with two parts.

questions.question: One person, five ___.
questions.explanation_en: The plural of person is people.

questions.question: "I can count on my brother." means ___.
